# Summer's Unhurried Harvest

## Scripture
*"There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens."* — Ecclesiastes 3:1

## Reflection

In late August, the night sky tells a quiet story of transition. The Summer Triangle—Vega, Deneb, and Altair—still blazes overhead, yet the constellations are already tilting westward. The brilliant stars of summer are slowly surrendering their reign to autumn's evening sky, and the Milky Way's luminous river arches across the heavens like a final summer blessing.

We often view celestial events through the lens of urgency—eclipses, meteor showers, comets that demand our immediate attention. But this week, the sky invites us to notice what takes its time. The stars don't rush their seasonal dance. Vega will still shine, just a little earlier each night, making way for what comes next.

There's a profound peace in remembering that God's timing is not our hurried schedule. The same hand that set the stars in their patient procession also orchestrates the seasons of our lives—including the ones that feel like long, unremarkable summers. Growth often happens beneath the surface, invisible to our anxious eyes, yet exactly on time.

Trust the unhurried work of the Gardener. The One who hangs the stars knows precisely when to release the harvest in your soul.

## Prayer
Patient Father, teach me to rest in Your timing. When I long for quick answers and visible progress, remind me that You are working faithfully in every season. Help me to watch the sky with wonder and my life with trust, knowing You who began this good work will complete it—in Your perfect time. Amen.
